title: Solving an absolute-value inequality
steps: An absolute value less than 5 means \(-5<2x+3<5\). Subtract 3 throughout, then divide by 2.

title: Projecting one vector onto another
steps: The scalar product is \(\mathbf u\cdot\mathbf v=1(2)+2(-3)=-4\), while \(|\mathbf v|^2=2^2+(-3)^2=13\). Multiply \(\mathbf v\) by their ratio.

title: Changing variables in an integral
steps: With \(x=5\sin\theta\), we have \(dx=5\cos\theta\,d\theta\) and \(25-x^2=25\cos^2\theta\). The endpoints become \(-\pi/6\) and \(\pi/6\).
Thus \(\dfrac{dx}{25-x^2}=\dfrac15\sec\theta\,d\theta\); the cosine is positive throughout these limits.

title: Bernoulli mean and variance
steps: The success probability is \(p=P(X=1)=2/3\). A Bernoulli variable has mean \(p\) and variance \(p(1-p)\).

title: Counting trigonometric solutions
steps: Write \(\sin x=\cos(\pi/2-x)\), then use the sum-to-product identity:
\[\cos5x+\sin x=2\cos(2x+\pi/4)\cos(3x-\pi/4).\]
The first factor gives \(x=\pi/8+k\pi/2\), with \(k=0,1,2,3\). The second gives \(x=\pi/4+k\pi/3\), with \(k=0,1,\ldots,5\). None coincide, so there are \(4+6\) distinct solutions.

title: Using odd symmetry in integration
steps: The function \(\tan^{-1}x\) is odd and \(x^2\) is even, so their product is odd. An odd integrand has zero integral between opposite limits.

title: Reading a slope field
steps: The slopes depend on the horizontal position only. They are zero on the \(y\)-axis, positive on both sides, and steeper as \(|x|\) grows. These are the features of \(x^2\).

title: Ordering collinear points
steps: Rearrange \(\mathbf c=3\mathbf a-2\mathbf b\) to obtain \(\mathbf a=(2/3)\mathbf b+(1/3)\mathbf c\). Both weights are positive and add to 1, so A is inside the segment BC.
answer: A: A lies between B and C.

title: Finding the angle between vectors
steps: Since \(\mathbf a+\mathbf b=-\mathbf c\), squaring the magnitudes gives \(49=9+25+2(3)(5)\cos\theta\). Hence \(\cos\theta=1/2\).

title: Second derivative of an inverse
steps: From \(f(g(x))=x\), differentiate twice: \(f'(g)g'=1\) and \(f''(g)(g')^2+f'(g)g''=0\).

title: Finding a rational inverse
steps: Set \(y=1-1/(x-2)\). Then \(1-y=1/(x-2)\), so \(x=2+1/(1-y)\). Exchange the input and output.

title: Factoring a trigonometric equation
steps: Use \(\sin2\theta=2\sin\theta\cos\theta\) to obtain \(\sin\theta(2\cos\theta-1)=0\).
The sine factor gives the endpoints 0 and \(\pi\); the other factor gives \(\cos\theta=1/2\), hence \(\theta=\pi/3\) in the required interval.

title: Integrating a trigonometric product
steps: The product-to-sum identity gives \(\sin3x\cos x=\tfrac12(\sin4x+\sin2x)\). Integrate each sine term, including its chain-rule divisor.

title: Sketching a scaled inverse cosine
steps: The input of inverse cosine must satisfy \(-1\le2x\le1\), so the domain is \([-1/2,1/2]\). Scaling its output by \(1/3\) gives the range \([0,\pi/3]\).
Draw a smooth decreasing curve through \((-1/2,\pi/3)\), \((0,\pi/6)\) and \((1/2,0)\). Include both endpoints; the tangents become vertical there.

title: Making vectors parallel
steps: The vector \((2,6)\) is twice \((1,3)\). The same scale factor must apply to both components.

title: Using sums and products of roots
steps: Put the fractions over a common denominator: \(1/(\alpha\beta)+1/(\alpha\gamma)+1/(\beta\gamma)=(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)/(\alpha\beta\gamma)\).
Vieta’s formulas give the sum \(-6/2=-3\) and product \(-(-1)/2=1/2\).

title: Integrating a squared cosine
steps: Reduce the power using \(\cos^2(3x)=(1+\cos6x)/2\). An antiderivative is \(x/2+\sin6x/12\).
The sine terms vanish at both \(x=\pi/6\) and \(x=\pi/3\). The remaining difference is \(\pi/6-\pi/12\).

title: Related rates in a sector
steps: The fixed area gives \(\tfrac12r^2\theta=10\). At \(r=4\), \(\theta=20/16=5/4\).
Differentiate with respect to time: \(r\theta\,dr/dt+\tfrac12r^2\,d\theta/dt=0\). Substituting \(d\theta/dt=2\) gives \(5\,dr/dt+16=0\).
answer: \(\dfrac{dr}{dt}=-3.2\text{ cm s}^{-1}\): the radius is decreasing.

title: Volume of revolution about the y-axis
steps: Express the radius of a horizontal disc in terms of its height: \(x=1/y\). Its area is \(\pi x^2=\pi/y^2\).

title: Induction with factorials
steps: Base case \(n=1\): the sum is 1 and \(2!-1=1\).
Assume \(\sum_{j=1}^{k}j(j!)=(k+1)!-1\). Adding the next term gives
This is precisely the required statement for \(k+1\). The base case and implication establish the identity for every positive integer.

title: Separating a differential equation
steps: Write \(dy/\sqrt{4-y^2}=dx\). Integration gives \(\sin^{-1}(y/2)=x+C\).
At \((x,y)=(0,1)\), \(C=\pi/6\). Take sine to obtain the solution on the increasing branch through the initial point.
The sine expression solves the original equation on \(-2\pi/3\le x\le\pi/3\); on this interval its cosine factor is non-negative.

title: Writing a trigonometric expression as one sine
steps: Expand \(2\sin(x-\alpha)=2\cos\alpha\sin x-2\sin\alpha\cos x\). Matching coefficients gives \(\cos\alpha=\sqrt3/2\) and \(\sin\alpha=1/2\).

title: Solving with a phase shift
steps: Part (i) turns the equation into \(2\sin(x-\pi/6)=1\).
For \(-\pi/6\le x-\pi/6\le11\pi/6\), sine equals \(1/2\) at \(\pi/6\) and \(5\pi/6\). Add \(\pi/6\) to each.

title: Choosing the correct solution branch
steps: Separate and integrate: \(y\,dy=5\,dx\), so \(y^2/2=5x+C\). The initial value gives \(C=8\), hence \(y^2=10x+16\).
The initial value is negative, so choose the negative square root. Exclude the endpoint where \(y=0\), because the original differential equation divides by \(y\).

title: Circular arrangements with a restriction
steps: Fix one guest to remove rotational duplicates. The unrestricted count is \(7!\).
For the forbidden arrangements, combine the two specified guests into one block. The resulting seven objects have \(6!\) circular arrangements, with 2 orders inside the block. Subtract these.

title: Angle between velocity and acceleration
steps: Differentiate the position vector: \(\mathbf v=(1,2t/9)\) and \(\mathbf a=(0,2/9)\).
The dot-product formula gives \(\cos(\pi/4)=2t/\sqrt{81+4t^2}\). The angle is acute, so \(t>0\).
Squaring yields \(1/2=4t^2/(81+4t^2)\), hence \(4t^2=81\). Keep the positive time.

title: Normal approximation to a binomial count
steps: With replacement, \(X\sim\operatorname{Bin}(100,p)\). Since \(100p=20\), \(p=0.2\) and \(\sigma=\sqrt{100(0.2)(0.8)}=4\).
The lower-tail probability is \(1-0.0668=0.9332\). The supplied normal table gives \(P(Z\le1.5)=0.9332\).
Using the standard normal approximation requested in the question, \((k-20)/4=1.5\).

title: Rearranging Pascal’s identity
steps: Use Pascal’s identity with \(n=m+1\) and \(r=R+1\): \(\binom{m+1}{R+1}=\binom mR+\binom m{R+1}\). Move the last term to the other side.

title: Telescoping a sum of binomial coefficients
steps: Apply part (i) with \(R=2000\). Each term \(\binom m{2000}\) becomes \(\binom{m+1}{2001}-\binom m{2001}\).
Summing for \(m=2000,\ldots,2050\), all intermediate terms cancel, leaving \(\binom{2051}{2001}-\binom{2000}{2001}\). The last term is zero because 2001 objects cannot be chosen from 2000.

title: Divisibility of a product of factors
steps: Among the positive factors of 60, only four are odd: 1, 3, 5 and 15. Any seven selected factors therefore include at least three even numbers, supplying more than the two factors of 2 needed.

Only six factors avoid a multiple of 3: 1, 2, 4, 5, 10 and 20. Likewise only six avoid a multiple of 5: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 12. Seven selections must therefore supply both a factor of 3 and a factor of 5.
Thus the product is divisible by \(2^2\times3\times5=60\).
answer: The product of any seven distinct positive factors of 60 is a multiple of 60.

title: Comparing horizontal projectiles
steps: Let \(OB=h\), so \(OA=kh\). Both particles start with zero vertical speed. Their respective flight durations are \(t_A=\sqrt{2kh/g}\) and \(t_B=\sqrt{2h/g}\).
They have the same horizontal range, so \(Ut_A=Vt_B\). Dividing gives \(V/U=t_A/t_B=\sqrt{k}\). The launch delay does not change either particle’s flight duration measured from its own launch.

title: Perpendicular clock hands
steps: Perpendicular vectors have zero dot product. Dividing that product by 2 and using \(\cos(A-B)=\cos A\cos B+\sin A\sin B\) gives \(\cos(11\pi t/360)=0\).
The first two positive angles are \(\pi/2\) and \(3\pi/2\). Therefore the times are \(180/11\) and \(540/11\) minutes after midnight.

title: Differentiating an inverse-trigonometric composite
steps: The chain rule gives \(f'(x)=-\cos x/\sqrt{1-\sin^2x}=-\cos x/|\cos x|\). The absolute value is essential.
Cosine is positive on \((0,\pi/2)\) and negative on \((\pi/2,\pi)\). At \(\pi/2\), the graph has a corner, so no derivative exists.

title: Combining roots with a tangent-sum identity
steps: Let the roots be \(p=\tan\alpha\), \(q=\tan\beta\), \(r=\tan\gamma\). Vieta gives \(p+q+r=-b\), \(pq+pr+qr=c\), and \(pqr=1-b-c\).
The three-angle tangent identity now gives \(\tan(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)=\dfrac{p+q+r-pqr}{1-pq-pr-qr}=\dfrac{-b-(1-b-c)}{1-c}=-1\). The assumption \(c\ne1\) allows this division.
The angle sums are \(-\pi/4+n\pi\). The first positive one occurs at \(n=1\).
